carried_from: data/color-contract-v1.json as it stood from 2026-09-10 to 2026-11-15 (color-channel-rule-v2-the-materials-are-the-ledgers-the-channels-are-the-owners-ruling-and-the-values-are-ours), which carried v1 (colour-role-rule-v1-the-roles-are-the-ledgers-and-the-values-are-ours) and v1's fixture, data/y-genesis-navigation-v1.js · color_contract · generated 2026-07-18. v2's five channels are carried forward, structure on a new material, and two are added: the Masoretic marks in gold and our layering in silver.

who_decided_what.the_ledger: Exodus names the materials — gold, silver and bronze (25:3), tekhelet, argaman, tola'at shani and shesh — over and over, and says what each was made into, and never once says what any of them looked like.
who_decided_what.the_owner: Which material carries which channel: the dyes ruled on 2026-09-10, the metals on 2026-11-15. The three dyes keep their channels. Gold is kept for the Masoretic marks alone ("gold as masoretic signs switching back to that"); bronze takes the frame that holds the page, the card, its outline and its pointer lines ("if bronze held the tent maybe that's the hud color"); silver is our layering, the blobs and the frames around joined words ("maybe silver would be like outlining all the compspan boxes since that's kind of our layering?"). Purple stays this project's own voice ("obviously purple stays as the commentary layer").
who_decided_what.this_page: Every hex value below, and every one before it. A role is recorded; a hex is a tradition, and the traditions disagree. No reader should come away thinking a hex code is attested — only that a channel was assigned, by a person, on a date.

channels.rule: A channel is not a decoration. It says who is speaking. The corpus speaks in tola'at shani, its reading speaks in tekhelet, this project speaks in argaman; the metals carry no voice of their own: gold is only ever a Masoretic mark, bronze is the frame that holds the page, and silver is the layer this project draws over the text.

text_as_written.carries: The Hebrew of the corpus, the letters as the source has them. Carried as a wash behind the letters and not in them: since 2026-09-10 every glyph on this page is argaman, and the ink says nothing about whose words these are.
text_as_written.how_it_is_carried: A wash the width of the word, under the glyph. It lifts while the reader is holding the word and comes back when they let go.
text_as_written.reads_as: the ink the Hebrew is written in, a quiet rose-red, with nothing behind the letters
text_as_written.held_as: muted: the material at a lower saturation than a glyph in it would be painted at, so a page of it is a page of words and not of color
text_as_written.dim_as: The dim red (--shani-dim) is never a word: it is the rail along a commentary, the edge of a source's tag, and the maqaf between a compound's pieces on a card's head in a work whose Masoretic marks are not drawn in gold (where they are, the maqaf is a mark and gold, on the line and on the card alike).

reading_as_shown.carries: The reading offered for a word: the English that comes from a dictionary this project holds a license to. Someone else's words about the corpus. Carried as a wash, the same as the corpus's own channel, because both are provenance and neither is ink.
reading_as_shown.note: Named and deliberately unused until today. v1 recorded that keeping it unused meant the day it appeared would be a decision somebody made rather than a color that crept in. This is that day, and the decision is recorded above.
reading_as_shown.how_it_is_carried: A wash behind the reading in a book. On the door, where a whole card IS one book's reading, the card carries it and the reading inside is not washed twice.
reading_as_shown.reads_as: the ink the reading is written in, a quiet blue, with nothing around it
reading_as_shown.held_as: muted: the material at a lower saturation than a glyph in it would be painted at, so a page of it is a page of words and not of color
reading_as_shown.pressed_as: One blue at two shades, a regular and a dim, and no bold (the owner, 2026-10-10: "id probably go regular and dim. i dont like our bold that much"; this supersedes 2026-10-03, "similar to our logo id have 2 blues: a bold and a regular", whose "maybe the letters bold too" stands as the weight). A reading at rest and a reading pressed are the same regular blue (--tekhelet). Pressed, it is worn bold inside the pressed cell (channels.reader_selection.pressed_cell), 3.83:1 on the pressed linen, the same as the open word's reading on the line. Never a blue fill.
reading_as_shown.dim_as: The dim blue (--tekhelet-dim) is never a reading: it is only the + between a reading's parts, which it tells apart from a + inside a reading's own words.

our_own_voice.carries: Sentences this project wrote: rule statements, counting notes, captions, obligation lines, what a demonstration says about itself, and every line saying a record holds nothing here. This is the page's INK — all of it — so our voice is the unmarked case and everything a reader sees marked is a departure from us into someone else's words.
our_own_voice.why: The owner's ruling. Once red is the text and blue is the reading, the project's own prose is the one voice left without a material, and it is the voice a reader most needs to be able to tell apart from the other two.
our_own_voice.how_it_is_carried: The ink, everywhere, in two purples and no more (the owner, 2026-10-10: "personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen"; "titles get regular and text gets dim ... id probably go regular and dim"): the regular (--argaman) for titles, values and what is under the reader's hand; the dim (--argaman-dim) for running text, notes, labels, and links and controls at rest, held at body-text contrast. A line saying something is absent, withheld, refused or does not reconcile is the dim, in italic where it stands in for a name or a value; the saturated argaman it had of its own from 2026-09-10 is folded in.
our_own_voice.reads_as: the ink itself — every glyph on the page is this

masoretic_marks.carries: The Masoretic marks, the vowel points and the accents, wherever the page draws them by their class (masoretic-marks-rule-v1-every-mark-is-gold-by-its-class-never-by-a-code-point-range): on the line and at the head of a card. The letters under them keep the corpus's red. Nothing else on the page is gold.
masoretic_marks.why: The owner, 2026-11-15: "gold as masoretic signs switching back to that" (the marks have been gold since 2026-10-11: "every mark gold, vowels included"), and of its shade: "i still prefer the pale/real gold, not the orangey one".
masoretic_marks.reads_as: the ink of the vowel points and the accents, and of nothing else: a real gold, never the orange one, over letters that keep the corpus's red
masoretic_marks.in_exodus: The first metal named (25:3), and the one the holiest things are made of or covered with: the ark, the mercy seat and its cherubim, the table, the lampstand (chapter 25). The one metal worked into the cloth itself: beaten into thin plates and cut into threads, to be worked into the tekhelet, the argaman, the tola'at shani and the shesh (39:3). Thread, never a ground. Exodus never says what it looked like.

structure.carries: The frame that holds the page: the card (the hud) and its outline, the pointer lines from a held word to its card, the boxes of the apparatus (verse labels, the edges of buttons, pills and switches) and the rules between parts. The frame a reading sits in.
structure.in_process: Bronze never terminates. It is the box, never the thing in the box, and a word is never left bronze: it resolves into a text color or a reading color.
structure.reads_as: line work: the card's outline and its pointer lines, rules, borders and boxes; and, in its regular, the ink of the apparatus's numbers (a word's address on its card, the card numbers on the line), which were gold ink before; never any other ink
structure.in_exodus: The court's metal and the tent's fittings: the altar of burnt offering, covered with bronze, and its vessels, grate, rings and poles (27:2–6; 38:2–7); the sockets of the court's pillars (27:10, 17–18); the laver and its stand (30:18; 38:8); the altar's bronze grate, the court's pillars and sockets, and the pegs of the tabernacle and of the court with their cords (35:16–18); every peg of the tabernacle and of the court (27:19; 38:20); and the bronze of the offering, made into the sockets of the tent's door, the altar, the sockets of the court and of its gate, and all the pegs (38:29–31). What held the tent and its hangings in place. Exodus never says what it looked like.
structure.moved_from: gold, from 2026-09-10 (the v2 record: "Gold is not a final color: it is an in-process color — huds, boxes, the frame") to 2026-11-15, when the owner gave the frame to bronze ("if bronze held the tent maybe that's the hud color") and kept gold for the Masoretic marks. The fixture this contract descends from (data/y-genesis-navigation-v1.js, 2026-07-18) valued structure gold; that half of it is retired here, as its two surfaces were on 2026-09-10.
structure.held_apart_from_gold_by: Hue and saturation, measured (the owner, 2026-11-15: "bronze is distinctly not orange, and silver is distinct too"): the bronze is a brown at hue 28° and 30% saturation; the gold of the marks is a yellow at hue 46°. A bronze made darker or lighter for contrast keeps its hue and its low saturation.

our_layering.carries: What this project draws over the text to show how its words join: the blob that ties a word to its English, and the frame drawn around words joined into one card (a compspan, a megacompspan). Ours, as the purple is, but drawn rather than written.
our_layering.why: The owner, 2026-11-15: "maybe silver would be like outlining all the compspan boxes since that's kind of our layering?" … "oh interesting you're saying blobing is our commentary, yea i guess that is the big one, true".
our_layering.reads_as: line work only: the outline of a blob and the frame around joined words, never ink and never a ground; the blob's own ground is the pressed linen
our_layering.in_exodus: The tabernacle's footing and its fastenings: the sockets under the boards of the tabernacle (26:19–25), the hooks and bands of the court's pillars (27:10–11; 38:10–12, 17, 19), and the silver of those counted, cast into the sockets of the sanctuary and the veil and made into the hooks, the caps and the bands (38:25–28). Exodus never says what it looked like.

reader_selection.carries: What this reader has opened, chosen, pressed or armed among the page's own controls: the verse number the address names, the mode pressed, the chapter opened. Nothing wears it at rest, and no word wears it at all.
reader_selection.in_process: A selection is the most in-process thing on the page, so the page's own controls take the bronze at their edge while the reader's hand is on them, drawn twice as heavy when pressed. Words are not controls: what a reader sees under a held word is the word's own channel, weighted, never a metal. The edge at rest is the dim bronze and the edge under the hand the regular, a step darker at the same hue, as the two golds did from 2026-10-10.
reader_selection.held_apart_from_structure_by: Hue and weight. Structure is bronze and does not move; a selection is purple, bold, and the only thing on the page that appears and disappears under the reader's hand.
reader_selection.moved_from: v1 valued this electric_blue, and from 2026-09-09 it was gold at its amber value. Blue became the reading, so a blue selection said "selected" and "English" in one color; then the owner, 2026-10-03, on amber pills: "idk if turning purple to gold is a clear way to highlight toggle pills et al, maybe bold purple would be better?" A pressed control is now this project's own purple, worn bold. From 2026-10-10 it is the regular purple itself, worn bold; the press is carried by the weight and the pressed cell, not by a purple deeper than the ink.
reader_selection.reads_as: ink on the page's own controls under the reader's hand, worn bold, and gone when they let go; a held word keeps its own ink inside a bronze box
reader_selection.held_word: A word the reader is holding is boxed in bronze — the whole block, Hebrew and reading together, an outline three pixels out — and the card is that box projected forward: two bronze lines from the box's far corners to the card's near corners. Nothing is filled and no ink changes (owner, 2026-09-11, drawn on a screenshot; the box and its lines were gold until 2026-11-15). A held word never takes the purple of a pressed control.
reader_selection.held_apart_from_our_voice_by: Weight and behavior: our voice at rest is the regular weight of the page's ink; a selection is the same purple pressed bold, and only while it is pressed.
reader_selection.pressed_cell: One rule for every pressed or highlighted cell, pill or control (the owner, 2026-10-03: "i wouldnt retrace pills from gold to blue. you keep jumping rules. id: 1. darken the linen backdrop on a highlighted cell, 2. bolden the gold, 3. bolden the blue text"): its border stays the frame's metal, drawn twice as heavy (gold when this was ruled, bronze since 2026-11-15); its linen darkens one step (--press-wash); its letters are bold in their own ink at its regular shade: the regular blue for a reading, the purple for a control (the owner, 2026-10-10: "i dont like our bold that much"; the bold is the weight, not a deeper color). No cell is ever filled with a color.

faces.rule: One face. The courtyard: linen hangings in daylight. There is nothing here for a reader to choose and nothing kept on the device.

day.commentary_set_apart_by: Its red rail and its frame, not a ground of its own. The commentary's parchment, decided 2026-09-10 and carried from the v1 fixture, was folded into the ground on 2026-10-10 under the owner's three linens ("personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen").
day.linens: Three, and no more (the owner, 2026-10-09: "maybe linen should have 3 shades?"; 2026-10-10: "personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen"): the ground (--bg), on which the page, a card, a pill, a panel and a commentary at rest stand; the cell (--cell-wash), a glaze laid on the ground behind a word and its reading, which a hover and a chip also wear; and the pressed linen (--press-wash), which every pressed cell wears and the blob between a word and its English shares. A glaze is never laid on another glaze, and a veil of the ground is the ground.

faces.what_was_dropped: The tent's dark face, a purple ground under its coverings, which v1 and v2 both carried and this edition served until today. The owner dropped it. It is not deprecated or left behind a flag: the palette, the toggle, the stored preference and every rule written for it are gone, because a half-removed face paints some elements from a palette nothing else uses, and that is worse than either state.
faces.what_this_costs: A reader whose device is set to dark now gets linen. color-scheme is declared light so the browser does not hand its own dark chrome to a light page. Nothing about the channels moved: they were tuned on this face, and this is the face that was called right.
faces.note: The two-faced rule read: 'the courtyard hangings are linen in daylight, and the tent is dark under its coverings.' Half of that sentence described something this edition no longer does, so the sentence went rather than being left standing over an absence.
faces.no_second_face_on_2026_11_15: A bronze night face was drawn on 14 and 15 November and set aside by the scheme the owner gave the metals ("but then we wouldn't change the linen background or add a darkmode"). One face stands.

the_woven_name.rule: The name is dyed in the page's own materials (the owner, 2026-10-10: "my main point is uniform coloring between logo and site"), each word woven, and no word's thread runs into another's.
the_woven_name.fire: tola'at shani, its threads crossed with themselves; the flame over its i the same, its heart gold crossed with gold
the_woven_name.and: gold crossed with bronze; no thread of fire's red or of hail's blue runs into it (the owner, 2026-11-15: "i kind of like none. what if we did gold/bronze woven on and, and purple and silver woven on .com")
the_woven_name.hail: tekhelet, its threads crossed with themselves; the hailstone over its i the same
the_woven_name.dot_com: argaman crossed with silver, its dot woven with it (the owner, 2026-11-15: "2 but i'd probably weave it tighter")
the_woven_name.weave: a plain weave in an X: warp and weft cross, each thread over one and under the next, at ±60° from level (the slant the threads ran at before), 21 font units between threads (42 before) (the owner, 2026-11-15: "x steep tighter still looks cool")
the_woven_name.no_orange: every gold in the name is the real gold of the marks and its paler body, never the orange gold of before
the_woven_name.drawn_by: tools/build-wordmark-v1.py, from settings that are data: the weave, its angle, the distance between threads, each word's warp and weft, and the dot

drawing.how_it_is_held: tools/check-woven-name-v1.mjs holds the drawing to this pin, its threads to the page's own values, and every page that shows the name to the file; a redraw the owner has approved moves the pin in the same change

note: Linen is not glare: the day ground sits below paper white and its ink is warm, not black. Shesh is the cloth the whole page is written in, which is why it is the neutral and not a channel.
what_changed_after_v2_was_written: On 2026-09-11 the held word stopped taking amber: it deepens its own wash instead (channels.reader_selection.held_word), and amber stays with the page's own controls. On 2026-09-11, off six mockups rendered on the real page, the owner chose the fourth: the ink carries the channel again, held muted — Hebrew in a quiet rose-red, its reading in a quiet blue with a gold hairline, no wash behind either — and the page's one ink, argaman, stays on everything that is ours. The held word lifts (a touch larger, a soft shadow) and the card pops out from under it; nothing held is filled. The washes of 2026-09-10 are retired; the one place a channel is filled is the pressed pill on the card, which is the reading's own ink with the linen for letters. Later on 2026-09-11 the held word stopped lifting and took the gold box instead, with the two projection lines to the card; the readings lost their boxes; the Hebrew at the head of the card is the same rose as on the line. On 2026-10-10 the palette was folded to two of each color and three linens (the owner: "personally i dont see a gain from more than 2/2/2/2 and 3 linen"; "id probably go regular and dim. i dont like our bold that much"; "my main point is uniform coloring between logo and site"). Gold is two: the dim at rest on every frame, chip and line, on the Masoretic marks and on the and of the name; the regular under the reader's hand. The amber, the name's own brighter gold and the hover's brown are gone. The purple is two: the regular for titles, values and what is pressed, the dim for running text, notes, labels and links. The red and the blue are two each, and a pressed reading is the regular blue worn bold. The woven name is dyed in the same pairs. On 2026-11-10 the owner formalized the values of three channels' materials from a set of six tabernacle swatches shown to the owner the day before ("i do want to formalize the correct blue, scarlet and purple chatgpt showed"): tekhelet #23558a, argaman #642460, tola'at shani #a52035, read off the owner's screenshot, which printed no hex. Each keeps its two shades: the regular is the swatch, and the dim is the regular thinned with the linen until it reads as the dim before it read. The channels, who speaks in which, did not move; the argaman turned from a violet toward a red-purple, and the red and the blue deepened. The gold, the linens and the color of the Masoretic marks were left as they were for the owner to choose from screenshots.
what_changed_on_2026_11_15: The owner gave the metals channels of their own, in the order the words came (wip/2026-11-15/the-palette/THE-OWNERS-WORDS-2026-11-15.md, words 10 to 19): gold back to the Masoretic marks, bronze to the frame that holds the page, silver to our layering; the linen and the three dyes as they were; no dark face. Values, all this page's: the marks' gold #967c26, the same yellow as the swatch's pale gold #d3af37 made darker (hue 46°, 60%; 3.0:1 on the linen, as the orange read 3.4:1: the owner took #a48829 first, 2.6:1, then, shown it beside the orange and a step darker, the darker, "if you want to do a shade darker gold thats fine"), in place of the orange #a06c10 (hue 38°); bronze in two shades, as every color keeps a pair (the owner, 2026-10-10: "id probably go regular and dim"): the dim #7f6044 at rest (hue 28°, 30%; 4.3:1) and the regular #6d523a under the hand and as the numbers' ink (the same hue and saturation; 5.4:1, so a number reads as text must); silver #6e7378, the swatch #7c8187 (hue 213°, 4%) made a step darker at its own hue, because a frame's line sits on the blob's pressed linen too, where the swatch read 2.5:1 and a line a reader needs must reach 3:1 (3.6:1 on the linen, 3.0:1 on the pressed linen). The woven name's threads, each an edge and a body: gold #967c26 and #d3af37, bronze #7f6044 and #9a7656, silver #6e7378 and #b4b8bd (its edge the page's silver, so the name and the page keep one silver), argaman #642460 lit with #753c6d. No hex here is attested; each is a choice made on a screen and kept.
